+-- Differences from a literal translation:
+--  * Dynamic SQL: EXECUTE (@SQL) with QUOTENAME -> EXECUTE format() with %I; the #CurrentValue temp table that carries
+--    MAX() out of the dynamic statement -> EXECUTE ... INTO.
+--  * sys.sequences.current_value -> the sequence's own last_value column. pg_sequences.last_value is not the same: it is

+    -- Ensures that the next sequence value is above the maximum value of the supplied table column
+    IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_sequences AS s WHERE s.schemaname = 'sequences' AND s.sequencename = sequence_name) THEN
+        EXECUTE format('SELECT last_value FROM sequences.%I', sequence_name)
+            INTO current_sequence_maximum_value;

@@ engineOutput line 24 / final line 33 @@
+    EXECUTE format('SELECT COALESCE(MAX(%I), 0) FROM %I.%I',
+                   column_name,
+                   lower(schema_name),
+                   lower(regexp_replace(table_name, '([a-z0-9])([A-Z])', '\1_\2', 'g')))
-    EXECUTE format('SELECT COALESCE(MAX(%I), 0) FROM %I.%I', column_name, schema_name, table_name)
notes: Dynamic SQL: EXECUTE (@SQL) with QUOTENAME becomes PL/pgSQL EXECUTE format() with %I. The #CurrentValue temp table that carries MAX() out of the dynamic statement becomes EXECUTE ... INTO.

Identifier mapping follows this project's PostgreSQL naming: schema lower case, table snake_case, column and sequence names quoted as in SQL Server. The source resolves names case-insensitively (CI collation); the PostgreSQL version needs the names in their declared case. Only correctly cased names are generated, so case-insensitive name resolution is not claimed.
sys.sequences.current_value maps to the sequence relation's last_value (measured: start value before first use, last value issued after use, restart value after RESTART WITH).
Step 3 is the state form: the next value each sequence issues after the call is compared. Sequences are recreated per sample at generated start values, with 0-3 values consumed first.
Harness-only table Harness.SequenceStart carries the generated sequence start values; the object does not read it.

Verified in an isolated scratch database: the original T-SQL is deployed unchanged; tables contain only the columns the object references, with no foreign key constraints and no pre-existing rows. Every foreign-key column is indexed on both engines (a modelling assumption for the runtime step).
Step 4 is n/a for objects that change data (ruling 2026-11-12): each call changes the data it reads, so repeated timed runs on the same data are not the same work.

trapsCovered: state after the call (every row of the changed tables) and the error outcome
mutantsDetected: reads pg_sequences.last_value (NULL after a restart or before first use)
restarts at the maximum instead of maximum + 1
empty table maximum NULL instead of 0

effort.engineVersion: model selected dynamically by Kiro; exact model/version not exposed in the session
